chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from one who narrated it, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام or Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a man who had confessed against himself to sexual immorality. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to his companions, "Come to me tomorrow with your faces covered." So they came to him with their faces covered, and he said, "Whoever has done the like of what he did, let him not stone him, and let him depart."
He said: "So some of them departed and some remained, and those of them who remained stoned him."

key_terms.بِالْفُجُورِ: to grave sexual immorality in this legal context
key_terms.فَانْصَرَفَ: then he departed or turned away
key_terms.يَرْجُمْهُ: stone him as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام handle the stoning punishment for a man who confessed to zinā?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a case brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام involving a man who confessed to sexual immorality and the implementation of rajm. It highlights judicial procedure, the moral gravity of carrying out punishment, and the discernment exercised by the Imam عليه السلام in such matters.
